Auto-generated summary (brief):
Redwood did a migration demo showing parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together APIs to Redwood API. Discussion covered model endpoint mappings, streaming and function-calling equivalents, embeddings differences, cost/latency tradeoffs, and private deployment options (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Customer asked for benchmarks, parity mapping doc, and a pilot plan.

Topics discussed:
- Parity mapping of completion/chat/embedding endpoints
- Streaming vs chunked responses and function/tool calling equivalents
- Tokenization and embedding dimensionality mismatches
- Quantization and latency optimizations (dedicated vs hosted)
- Security: SOC 2, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, audit logs
- Next steps: parity spreadsheet, pilot and benchmarks, pricing/commit options

Transcript:
[00:00] Ben (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Ben from Redwood, this is Ava our solutions engineer, we'll walk through the migration mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API and also show the Console and Optimize toolkit.
[00:12] Sam (CTO): Thanks, yeah we want to understand parity — we run across OpenAI and Together at the moment, a bit of Anthropic for certain tasks, so can you show how prompts and calls map and what breaks?
[00:24] Ava (SE): Absolutely. We'll start with the simple text generation parity, then encodings/embeddings, then streaming and function calling. We'll also flag places where behavior differs, like sampling defaults, stop tokens, and response formatting.
[00:36] Priya (ML Eng): Quick thing: our pipeline relies on embeddings at 1536 dims from OpenAI for semantic search. We need to know how Redwood embeddings line up and if there are vector dim mismatches.
[00:47] Ava: Good call. Redwood's embeddings currently supports the curated models that match 1536 outputs for the commonly used models; in the parity spreadsheet we'll map model-to-model names and dims. For cases where dimension differs we suggest a migration strategy — reindex or run conversion layer.
[01:02] Liam (Infra): And on networking — we can't send prod data to a shared tenancy in some cases. We want to see VPC or on-prem options and how KMS works.
[01:12] Ben: Yep, we'll cover Dedicated and Private — VPC peering and customer-managed KMS/HSM, audit logs. We'll drop the SOC 2 and pen-test artifacts after the call.
[01:25] Ava: Ok demo time. I'm sharing my screen — first the API parity matrix: you'll see OpenAI's "chat.completions" and Together's similar endpoint map to Redwood's /v1/chat/completions with a couple of query params that control routing to hosted/dedicated/backends. (inaudible)
[01:45] Sam: Does Redwood preserve function calling semantics? We use function calling heavily.
[01:49] Ava: Yes — Redwood implements function/tool calling compatible with OpenAI's shape; minor differences: we return tool calls with a slightly different metadata object, sometimes the field names are like tool_name vs name, small schema differences — nothing breaking. We'll provide a snippet showing the exact mapping.
[02:10] Priya: What about response streaming? We rely on stream delta tokens for lower latency UI.
[02:14] Ava: Streaming is supported; Redwood streams SSE/HTTP2 and also the SDK has a streaming hook. One difference is batching under the hood: Redwood sometimes batches micro-requests for cost efficiency which can add 20-50ms depending on concurrency and batch window, but you can opt out or pin-to-dedicated for minimum jitter.
[02:36] Sam: So we should expect slightly variable tail latency on hosted?
[02:39] Ava: On hosted, yes, if you're on the free/shared pool. Dedicated or Private gives predictable latency and you can set SLOs. The Optimize tooling can suggest batching window  and quantization profiles to hit your cost targets while keeping p95 under X ms.
[02:55] Ben: Quick parity example — OpenAI call with model 'gpt-4o-mini' would map to Redwood model alias 'gpt4o-mini-open' or to a vendor-backed hosted variant. We'll include exact model aliases in the spreadsheet.
[03:12] Priya: Any differences in tokenization? We saw small token counts differ between OpenAI and Together which impacts billing.
[03:19] Ava: Yes tokenizers vary; Redwood reports tokens using the model's tokenizer. In the mapping doc we include tokenization deltas per model and recommend re-calibrating cost estimates. For immediate parity we suggest running a tokenization pass over a sample of your prompts.
[03:38] Liam: For private infra, does Redwood support on-prem air-gapped installs?
[03:42] Ben: Yes, we have an on-prem package and VPC/private control plane options. The on-prem does require additional ops support and a licensing conversation; we'll scope that if you want to go down that route.
[03:57] Sam: Security: SAML SSO integration? RBAC? Audit logs?
[04:01] Ava: We integrate with SAML/SSO and OIDC. RBAC is available in Console, and detailed audit logs are stored based on retention policy (we can push longer retention as an add-on). KMS integrations for encrypting cached content and keys are standard — note that some customers prefer customer-managed keys in dedicated/private deployments.
[04:21] Priya: Performance — can we run a benchmark to compare p50/p95 between Together's hosted and Redwood hosted?
[04:27] Ava: Yes we have a benchmark harness you can run with your prompts. We'll run an initial benchmark on Redwood hosted and also on Dedicated to show differences. We'll provide the script and a test harness for the pilot.
[04:40] Ben: On cost — Redwood pricing is usage-based; for migration we can model the monthly token estimate and show a delta. Reserved capacity (Dedicated) gives unit price reductions. We'll send a cost model sheet.
[04:54] Sam: Any gotchas around embeddings — indexing, vector store compat? We use Pinecone for now.
[05:00] Ava: Embeddings are standard float vectors; Redwood exports are compatible with Pinecone/FAISS/Weaviate. The only gotcha is dim mismatch or norm behavior; we'll include a compatibility section.
[05:12] [small crosstalk] Priya: Also curious about reranking/semantic search workflows — do you offer built-in rerank endpoints or do we need to compose?
[05:20] Ava: We have convenience endpoints in the Optimize toolkit for reranking and caching patterns; but most teams compose embeddings + re-rank via Redwood's reranker model recommendations. We'll demo that in the pilot if you'd like.
[05:34] Liam: Logging and PII — do you support redaction before logs hit your system?
[05:38] Ava: On hosted we offer optional automatic PII redaction in logs. For Private/on-prem you can keep logs locally. We'll surface the log retention and redaction controls in Console.
[05:50] Ben: Let's walk through a sample curl migration — Ava, can you paste the OpenAI example and show Redwood equivalent?
[05:54] Ava: [shares snippet] OpenAI: curl openai... model=gpt-4o-mini prompt=... Redwood equivalent: curl api.redwood.ai/v1/chat with model alias and headers x-redwood-deployment: hosted, body shape basically the same. Example: {
  "model": "gpt4o-mini-open",
  "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}],
  "max_tokens": 512
}
[06:25] Priya: And function call example?
[06:27] Ava: [shares] You keep functions array, Redwood will return a call like {"name":"get_customer","arguments":"{...}"} — tiny schema name differences but same workflow.
[06:40] Sam: What about rate limits and quotas — we have spikes from automations that need bursting.
[06:46] Ben: We can size Dedicated to handle baseline throughput and configure burst pools; hosted has quotas but we can support burst policies for enterprise. We'll include autoscale and burst details in the doc.
[06:58] Priya: A question on quantization — does Redwood offer int8 execution that preserves accuracy?
[07:02] Ava: Yes, we support Q8/JIT quantization paths in the runtime and Optimize will recommend quantization profiles per model/workload. The recommendation also includes expected latency/cost tradeoffs and perf regressions to watch for.
[07:18] Sam: Ok next steps?
[07:20] Ben: Recap — we'll send: parity mapping spreadsheet, sample curl/snippets, SOC2+pen-test, pilot plan and benchmark harness, and initial cost model. Ava will run an initial latency test and share results. Customer to provide sample prompt sets and expected token volumes.
[07:35] Priya: Sounds good. Can we get the parity doc and sample scripts within 3 days?
[07:40] Ben: Yes we'll aim for 2026-01-18.
[07:44] Liam: Also loop in our security lead for the scoping call on private deployment.
[07:48] Ben: Will do.
[07:50] [wrap up] Ben: Thanks everyone for the thoughtful questions — we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the scoping call.
